name: Lymphomatoid Papulosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Chimenti et al. Diagnostic Criteria for Lymphomatoid Papulosis

criteria.description: Recurrent, self-healing papulonodular skin lesions with central necrosis or ulceration
Histopathological evidence of CD30-positive atypical lymphoid infiltrate
Chronic, recurrent course with spontaneous resolution and new lesion development
Exclusion of other cutaneous T-cell lymphomas and systemic lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent papulonodular lesions with characteristic histopathology (CD30 positivity) and chronic relapsing course
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires clinicopathologic correlation and exclusion of other lymphoproliferative disorders.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent erythematous papulonodular skin lesions with central necrosis
searchTerms: repeated red skin bumps with central dead tissue

pathognomonic.symptomName: Spontaneous resolution of skin lesions leaving varioliform scars
searchTerms: skin lesions heal leaving pitted scars
spontaneous skin lesion resolution with scarring

pathognomonic.symptomName: CD30-positive atypical lymphoid infiltrate on skin biopsy
searchTerms: skin biopsy showing CD30-positive abnormal lymphocytes
atypical lymphoid cells with CD30 marker in skin
CD30+ lymphoid infiltrate in skin tissue

common.symptomName: Erythematous papules and nodules distributed on trunk and extremities
searchTerms: red bumps and nodules on body and limbs
erythematous papules on trunk and arms
raised red skin lesions on extremities
pitted scars after skin lesion healing
small swollen lymph nodes in area

occasional.symptomName: Fever associated with extensive skin involvement
searchTerms: fever linked to extensive skin involvement

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of skin lesions

searchTerms: feeling slightly tired when symptoms worsen

rare.notes: Occurs in a minority of cases over long-term follow-up

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing CD30-positive atypical lymphoid cells
Normal peripheral blood counts in most cases
imaging: Imaging generally unremarkable unless systemic lymphoma suspected
PET-CT may be used to exclude systemic involvement
other: Clinical course characterized by recurrent self-healing lesions
Histopathologic overlap with other CD30+ lymphoproliferative disorders

distinguishingFeatures: Larger, persistent nodules or tumors without spontaneous resolution
Histopathology shows sheets of large anaplastic CD30+ cells
Patch and plaque stage lesions rather than papulonodular
Lack of CD30 positivity in early stages

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging or persistent nodules without resolution
Systemic symptoms such as unexplained weight loss or night sweats
Evidence of extracutaneous lymphadenopathy or organ involvement
references: Chimenti MS, et al. Lymphomatoid papulosis: clinical and histopathologic features. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018.
Willemze R, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005.
